title: KV260 AXI test at 30 MHz forced clock — clock-mismatch hypothesis REJECTED
context: The pl_clk0 probe (results/kv260_pl_clock_probe.json) found Kria's fclk framework snaps assigned-clock-rates=<40000000> to DIVISOR0=25 giving 60 MHz actual, mismatching the 40 MHz-synth bitstream. 50 MHz rebuild (results/kv260_bd_build_N64.json was updated; build at aac5ef79) produced a new bitstream with ~20.56 ns critical path. This experiment tested whether forcing an on-hardware clock that gives POSITIVE slack for the new bitstream eliminates the hang.

sequence.result: 0x01011900 — DIVISOR0=25, actual 60 MHz — fclk ignored the 50 MHz overlay hint

sequence.action: recomputed critical path vs actual period: 20.56 ns path at 20 ns period = -0.56 ns slack (still negative)
devmem write DIVISOR0=50 (for 30 MHz exact, ~12 ns positive slack)
attempt UIO SPIN_COUNT readback with 3s SIGALRM + 5s timeout backstop
sequence.result: ssh connection timed out — kria unreachable

fclk_behavior_summary: Kria's fclk framework IGNORES overlay assigned-clock-rates hints entirely. Tested at build target 40 MHz -> register shows DIVISOR0=25 (60 MHz). Tested at build target 50 MHz -> register STILL shows DIVISOR0=25 (60 MHz). The register content is identical (0x01011900) in both cases regardless of overlay request. Direct register writes via devmem DO persist when no loadapp is in flight.

hypotheses_state.hypothesis: RTL AXI-Lite protocol deadlock on split channels
Clock-mismatch: hardware runs bitstream at higher frequency than synth target, setup timing violated, AXI flops metastable
hypotheses_state.by: Tested at 30 MHz forced clock — ~12 ns of positive slack for a 50-MHz-constraint bitstream. First AXI read STILL hung the PS. If setup timing were the cause, positive slack would make the flops sample cleanly. It did not.

hypotheses_state.hypothesis: SmartConnect protocol checker upstream panics on a protocol detail not reproduced in bare-DUT simulation
hypotheses_state.next_test: Extend the xsim testbench to instantiate an axi_protocol_checker between the master BFM and the DUT, or wrap the sampler in a SmartConnect exactly matching the BD

hypotheses_state.hypothesis: Clock switch DURING active PL — devmem DIVISOR write caused a clock glitch that metastably latched proc_sys_reset, leaving the sampler permanently held in reset (explains current-session hang but not original Exp 661 hangs which did NOT have a mid-run clock write)
hypotheses_state.next_test: After power-cycle: probe PL0_REF_CTRL BEFORE loadapp, write DIVISOR0=50 THEN loadapp, see if clock persists through load and AXI works

hypotheses_state.hypothesis: proc_sys_reset wiring bug in build_bd.tcl — ARESETN never actually reaches the sampler, permanently holding it in reset
hypotheses_state.next_test: Use Vivado's write_debug_probes + ILA to add an observation point on the sampler's S_AXI_ARESETN pin and confirm it goes high after loadapp

hypotheses_state.hypothesis: AXI ACLK signal is not actually connected to the sampler in the BD, even though the IP integrator reports the connection
hypotheses_state.next_test: Read the post-route netlist and grep for the s_axi_aclk net; verify it is driven by clk_pl_0 and not accidentally tied low

consolation: We eliminated three of the initial hypotheses with clean evidence. The remaining set is smaller and each remaining hypothesis has a concrete next test that doesn't risk the board.
operator_action_required: Power-cycle the Kria (third time this work session). When back up, the safest next experiment is to read the BD's routed netlist in Vivado post-route to inspect the AXI clock and reset connections, rather than another on-hardware attempt.
